title: Futures Atlas evidence item (inbox submission)
description: One public fact per file under ledger/inbox/. The file name must be <id>.json. Reviewer-only fields (kind, source_tier, confidence, review) are added when an item is promoted to ledger/reviewed/ and are NOT allowed here. Summary, reasoning and counterpoint are released under CC BY 4.0.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. Bumped with a CHANGELOG entry.

id.description: EV-<published as YYYYMMDD>-<short-kebab-slug>, e.g. EV-20261002-framework-revision. The date part must equal `published`.

archive_url.description: Optional archive copy (Wayback Machine or archive.today). Reviewers create one if missing.

sources.description: Optional corroborating sources for the SAME event (one event = one item). Extra sources raise reviewer confidence; they never add weight.

contributors.description: Optional extra credited handles (e.g. a later simultaneous submission merged in as a source). The first submitter stays in submitted_by.

published.description: Publication date of the source, or the date the fact happened, YYYY-MM-DD. The item counts only in the week of this date. Not before 2022-11-30, not in the future.

title.description: Headline or document title as published (may contain proper names).

summary.description: 1-3 neutral sentences: what happened, with numbers and dates the source gives. No opinion, no forecast of your own, no country names (use neutral descriptors such as 'a top-3 compute jurisdiction'; country names belong in `detail`). CC BY 4.0.

detail.description: Optional: document number, page or table, named organisations or countries. Shown only in the expanded ledger entry.

roads.description: Road(s) the fact bears on. May be empty only if `endings` or `indicator` is given.

endings.description: Optional: ending(s) the fact speaks to directly. Most evidence bears on roads only.

indicator.description: Optional indicator id from INDICATORS.md, e.g. I-R4-03. Omit if unsure; the reviewer assigns one or marks the item as context only.

direction.description: Does the fact make the road(s)/ending(s) above more or less likely? Reviewers may change it and record it against the indicator statement.

reasoning.description: One sentence: why that direction. CC BY 4.0.

counterpoint.description: The strongest reason the fact may not mean what it seems to. 'none known' is allowed. CC BY 4.0.

source_type.description: paper = paper/preprint; news = news report; official = law, regulation, gazette, government statement; dataset = dataset or statistical release; company = system card, filing, blog, announcement; other.

access.description: How a reader reaches the source. 'paywall' requires `access_note`.

access_note.description: Required for paywalled sources: where a free copy, abstract or archive is, or which part is readable without paying.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag of the source, e.g. en, zh, fr, pt-BR.

submitted_by.description: gh:<GitHub handle> of the person responsible for the submission (also when an agent drafted it).

agent.description: Optional disclosure: the AI agent or tool that drafted the item, e.g. 'coding agent, model name'. Responsibility stays with submitted_by.

coi.description: Optional conflict-of-interest disclosure by industry category. No employer names.

licence.description: Summary, detail, reasoning and counterpoint are released under CC BY 4.0. The source itself keeps its own licence.

road.description: R1 Rival blocs with obedient AI; R2 Gradual disempowerment; R3 Incident -> coordinated restraint; R4 Race -> loss of control; R5 Broad diffusion; R6 Gradual adoption (AI as an ordinary technology, adopted slowly).
